title: Patch Watch Desk
one_liner: Monitoring and patching for small-business PHP/WordPress sites during the coming wave of AI-found vulnerabilities.
speaker: Peter Diamandis
context: AI-assisted researchers found decade-old critical PHP flaws that allowed takeover without a password. OpenAI warned that similar findings will rise sharply, and Alex cited Linux kernel developers expecting an 18-month onslaught.
customer: Freelance web designers and small agencies maintaining 10–100 WordPress/PHP client sites, plus local businesses running their own WordPress
problem: When critical flaws drop weekly, small site owners can't tell which of their sites run vulnerable PHP versions or packages, and they patch late or never.
revenue_model: About $15–$40 per site per month for monitoring plus emergency patching, or about $299 a month per agency for up to 25 sites (estimate)
why_now: AI vulnerability discovery is surfacing old bugs in legacy code faster than volunteers and small owners can react. The hosts expect the volume to grow sharply over the next 18 months.
first_steps: Build the free exposure checker and post it in WordPress freelancer communities
Manually audit 10 agency portfolios for free in exchange for testimonials
Package a 'critical CVE within 48 hours' patch guarantee and sell it to the first 3 agencies
cost_to_start: About 2 weeks and under $300; patching work is labour you can partly automate with AI coding tools
competition: Managed WordPress hosts and security plugins already cover parts of this. An agency-focused, AI-assisted patch service is a narrower niche.
risks: Hosting companies may auto-patch for free. Liability if a patched site breaks. The wave of findings may be shorter than predicted.

tool.title: Stack Exposure Checker
tool.one_liner: Paste your PHP version and composer.lock to see end-of-life status and known vulnerabilities.
tool.demo: The user pastes a PHP version and the contents of composer.lock or a package list. The page checks the PHP branch's support and end-of-life dates and queries known vulnerabilities for each package and version. It returns a prioritized table (critical first) with fixed-in versions and a client-ready summary the agency can send. Example mode loads a sample outdated stack.
tool.data_plan: Customer's own input. Keyless public APIs: endoflife.date for PHP support dates and the OSV.dev vulnerability query API for packages (Packagist ecosystem).
